extracted.intended_audience: GAP users and developers; mathematicians and programmers writing GAP code and library functions
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and conventions for writing, calling, and inspecting GAP functions and statements, including evaluation order, option passing, operator semantics, statement forms (if/while/for/repeat), control flow (break/continue/return), and function/meta utilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function call argument evaluation and formal parameter allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: The arguments arg-expr s are evaluated from left to right, and the values are assigned to the newly created variables corresponding to the formal arguments. The first value is assigned to the first formal argument, the second to the second, and so on. If the last formal argument has the name arg then the values of all actual arguments not assigned to the other formal parameters are stored in a list and assigned to arg.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New variables for formal locals are initially unbound; trying to evaluate them before assignment signals an error. If an identifier of a formal argument/local appears in the body it refers to the newly allocated variable. Examples: Fibonacci(11); nested function calls allowed as actual arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return/Procedure-call semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: If during execution of a function body a return statement with an expression is executed, execution terminates and the value of the function call is the return expression. If a return without expression is executed, execution terminates and the function call produces no value (procedure call). If the body completes without a return, the call produces no value (procedure call).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes function calls (return value) from procedure calls (no value). Procedures conventionally named as verbs; functions as nouns. return; and return expr; can also be used in break loops to resume execution after an error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options mechanism for function calls
rubrics_metrics.description: Options can be supplied to a function-call separated from positional arguments by a colon ':' and use syntax like record components. A component name may appear without a value, in which case the value true is silently inserted. Options are evaluated left to right, but only after all arguments have been evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options passed this way are pushed to the global options stack so they are visible to subsidiary calls (equivalent to PushOptions(rec(...)); call; PopOptions()). Any option may be passed to any function; the system provides no safeguard against misspelled option names. Example: Size(fpgrp : hard, tcselection := "external");

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality and inequality operators (= and <>)
rubrics_metrics.description: The operator = tests for equality and evaluates to true if operands are equal, false otherwise; <> tests for inequality. For each type the definition of equality is given in the respective chapter. Objects in different families are never equal (so = gives false, <> gives true).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equality semantics depend on object family/type (see respective chapters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordering operators (<, >, <=, >=) and their domain
rubrics_metrics.description: < denotes less than, <= less-or-equal, > greater than, >= greater-or-equal. For each kind of objects the definition of the ordering is given in the respective chapter. < implements a total ordering of objects and is not generally compatible with inclusion relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only certain kinds support cross-family ordering (rationals < cyclotomics < finite field elements < permutations < booleans < characters < lists). For other objects GAP does not provide <. You can define ordering for other objects by installing methods for the operation \< but this may conflict when loading other code. Useful for sorting and PositionSorted on mixed-element lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison operators associativity and precedence
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparison operators (including operator in (see 21.8)) are not associative, so expressions like a = b <> c = d are invalid; use parentheses. Comparison operators have higher precedence than logical operators but lower precedence than arithmetic operators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a * b = c and d is interpreted as ((a * b) = c) and d. Use parentheses to clarify intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic operators semantics (+, -, *, /, mod, ^)
rubrics_metrics.description: Arithmetic operators include +, -, *, /, mod, and ^. Their meanings depend on operand types. a + b denotes addition; a - b denotes addition with additive inverse; a * b denotes multiplication; a / b denotes multiplication by multiplicative inverse of b; a mod b defined specially for integer/rational operands; ^ denotes powering for multiplicative elements when right operand integer and various group actions/conjugation when group elements involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: mod for integers: a mod b is r in 0..|b|-1 with a = r + b q. For rationals a = m/n (coprime), a mod b defined so m congruent to r n modulo b; example 4/6 mod 32 equals 2/3 mod 32. Unary + ignored; unary - returns additive inverse. ^ is not associative (use parentheses), unary + and - are right associative, *, /, mod, +, - are left associative. Precedence: ^ highest, then unary +/-, then *,/,mod, then +,-. Arithmetic operators have higher precedence than comparisons and logicals. Advice: if in doubt use parentheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements overview and termination
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP programs consist of statements (assignments, procedure calls, if, while, repeat, for, break, continue, return). Every statement must be terminated by a semicolon. Statements have no value and are executed for effect; using expressions as statements is a syntax error. Empty statements are permitted and have no effect; a sequence of statements is a statement sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement sequences are terminated by keywords; simplest sequence is a single semicolon. Example shows syntax error when using '=' instead of ':=' for assignment in a statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment form and semantics (var := expr;)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment assigns the value of expr to var. var may be an ordinary variable, a list element selection list-var[int-expr], or a record component selection record-var.ident. Left-hand side may be arbitrarily complex; variables are untyped so any value can be assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If expr is a function call the function must return a value; otherwise an error is signalled and you enter a break loop. You can leave break loop with quit; or supply a return value. Examples demonstrate assigning into records and lists, and returning from a break loop to supply value for assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure calls and convention distinguishing functions vs procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure call syntax: procedure-var([args]); Procedure calls are executed like function calls. Conventionally a function returns a value (name is a noun) and a procedure produces effects but no value (name is a verb). GAP does not enforce a strict runtime distinction; some functions both return values and produce effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Read is a procedure (side effect), Append modifies a list; Sortex both sorts a list and returns the permutation.

rubrics_metrics.name: If statement syntax and semantics (if ... elif ... else ... fi)
rubrics_metrics.description: if bool-expr1 then statements1 { elif bool-expr2 then statements2 } [ else statements3 ] fi; Execution: evaluate bool-expr1; if true execute statements1 and finish; otherwise evaluate elifs in turn until one true; if none true and else present execute else; if no else do nothing. There is no dangling else: the fi keyword terminates the if.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If is not an expression (cannot be assigned). If one of the boolean expressions evaluates to a non-true/non-false value an error is signalled and a break loop entered; in the break loop return true; or return false; may be used to proceed as if expression had yielded that boolean. Examples illustrate nested if and else association.

rubrics_metrics.name: While loop semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: while bool-expr do statements od; The while loop evaluates bool-expr first; if false loop terminates immediately, otherwise execute statements and repeat. The while loop may execute zero times if condition false initially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If bool-expr does not evaluate to true or false an error is signalled and a break loop entered; return false; continues with next statement after the loop, return true; continues at statements (after which next evaluation may again error). A while loop may be left prematurely using break.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeat-until loop semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: repeat statements until bool-expr; Statements are executed first, then bool-expr is evaluated; if true loop terminates, otherwise repeat. Thus the loop body executes at least once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Error handling for boolean expression same as while (break loop). repeat can be left prematurely using break. Examples show summing squares until exceeding a bound.

rubrics_metrics.name: For loop semantics and variants
rubrics_metrics.description: for simple-var in list-expr do statements od; The body executes with simple-var bound to each element of list-expr in order. simple-var must be a simple variable (not a list element or record component). for over a range [from..to] is common; for over an iterator executes while not IsDoneIterator and uses NextIterator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalence to an internal while with loop_list and loop_index (but these are distinct per for-loop). If object in for is not a list or iterator GAP tries Iterator(object). Modifying the list during iteration can affect the loop (new elements may be iterated); assigning a new value to the variable holding the list has no influence on the ongoing loop. For loops can be left with break (useful with iterators). Examples illustrate behavior when list is modified during iteration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Break statement usage
rubrics_metrics.description: break; causes an immediate exit from the innermost loop enclosing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is an error to use break outside a loop. Examples show finding an element and exiting the loop; misuse gives syntax error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continue statement usage
rubrics_metrics.description: continue; causes the rest of the current iteration of the innermost loop to be skipped (move to next iteration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is an error to use continue outside a loop. Examples show skipping elements with a certain property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return statement detailed behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: return; terminates the innermost function call currently executing and returns no value; an error is signalled if no function is executing. return expr; returns the value of expr and terminates the function. Both forms may be used in break loops to continue after an error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: What happens with expr when used in break loops depends on the particular error. Examples refer to functions fib and Stack for illustration.

rubrics_metrics.name: SyntaxTree utility
rubrics_metrics.description: SyntaxTree(f) takes a GAP function f and returns its syntax tree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for introspection of function structure (section introduces tools to handle GAP syntax trees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Function inspection utilities (NameFunction, NumberArgumentsFunction, NamesLocalVariablesFunction)
rubrics_metrics.description: NameFunction(func) returns the name of a function (for operations the declared name, for functions the variable name first assigned to). If no name exists returns "unknown". NumberArgumentsFunction(func) returns number of arguments, -1 for operations, and for functions with varargs returns -1 times total number of parameters. NamesLocalVariablesFunction(func) returns list of argument names followed by local variables or fail for operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: NameFunction(SylowSubgroup) -> "SylowSubgroup"; NumberArgumentsFunction(function(a,b,c,...)) -> actual count; NumberArgumentsFunction(Size) -> 1; NumberArgumentsFunction(Sum) -> -1; NamesLocalVariablesFunction(function(a,b) local c; ...) -> ["a","b","c"].

rubrics_metrics.name: Source/location utilities (FilenameFunc, StartlineFunc, EndlineFunc, LocationFunc, PageSource)
rubrics_metrics.description: FilenameFunc(func) returns absolute path of file from which func was read or fail (compiled functions/operations). StartlineFunc/EndlineFunc return the start/end line numbers in the file (or fail if no filename). LocationFunc returns a string describing location using FilenameFunc and StartlineFunc or fail if unknown. PageSource(func[,nr]) shows source in pager starting slightly before func; for operations shows declaration; second arg selects which declaration; attempts to show C source for kernel functions; indicates if no source found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For interactively entered functions FilenameFunc returns "*stdin*". Examples show retrieving location of methods and displaying source.

rubrics_metrics.name: CallFuncList/CallFuncListWrap semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: CallFuncList(func, args) calls func with arguments given in the list args (args is unwrapped so it appears as several arguments). CallFuncListWrap(func, args) differs only in that it returns a list: empty if called function returned no value, otherwise a single-element list containing the returned value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for forwarding arguments when a function f is defined with a single formal argument arg (varargs captured as list). Examples: CallFuncList(\+, [6,7]) -> 13; CallFuncListWrap(x->x,[1]) -> [1]; CallFuncListWrap(function(x) end, [1]) -> [ ].

rubrics_metrics.name: MemoizePosIntFunction behavior and options
rubrics_metrics.description: MemoizePosIntFunction(function[,options]) returns a function that behaves like function but caches results for positive integer inputs. By default the cache can be flushed by FlushCaches(). The returned function by default accepts only positive integers. The function may call the underlying function more than once for an input (cache evictions, FlushCaches, or concurrency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options record supports: defaults (list to initialise cache entries), flush (boolean, whether FlushCaches empties cache), errorHandler (function called when non-positive-integer input passed; may raise error or return a value which is not cached). Example shows defaults and errorHandler usage and interaction with FlushCaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Null-returning and identity utility functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The library provides small utility functions that return fixed results or pass-through values: ReturnTrue(...), ReturnFalse(...), ReturnFail(...), ReturnNothing(...), ReturnFirst(...), IdFunc(obj).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ReturnTrue/ReturnFalse/ReturnFail/ReturnNothing accept any arguments and always return true/false/fail/nothing respectively. ReturnFirst returns its first argument (requires at least one arg). IdFunc returns its single argument. Useful as placeholders where syntax requires a function (e.g., family predicates in InstallMethod).

rubrics_metrics.name: Function types and families (IsFunction, FunctionsFamily)
rubrics_metrics.description: IsFunction(obj) is the category predicate for functions. FunctionsFamily is the family of all functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: IsFunction(x->x^2) -> true; IsFunction(Factorial) -> true; compiled function objects may not satisfy IsFunction as expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming conventions for functions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a variable name has several words the first letter of each word is capitalized. If the first part of a function name is a verb then the function may modify its arguments (procedural), otherwise it returns an object without changing arguments (functional). If name contains 'Of' the return value is information deduced from arguments (often attributes). 'By' indicates the return is built in a certain way from parts given as arguments; 'With' may guarantee generators equality. 'AsSomething' indicates return is an object interpreted 'as something' (e.g., AsGroup).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conventions help remember/guess library names. Examples: Append (verb, modifies list) vs Concatenation (noun, returns list). GeneratorsOfGroup returns generators; NaturalHomomorphismByNormalSubgroup constructs homomorphism by normal subgroup. Use 'With' to indicate guarantee about internal representation (GeneratorsOfStruct equals given generators).
